name: Lev Adair
life: Lev tested signs for a shop chain until it replaced his team. He opened his repair business with one bulb over the door and kept a private count of drivers who slowed down on the first evening. Monday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Lev looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: The switch worked. He'd unscrewed the bulb to see who would notice. I recognized the trick because I once did it to my shop sign. I left a spare on his kitchen table.
appearance: Lev is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in a moss-green cardigan with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand, Lev looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Lev can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Lev can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To leave a working spare without exposing the owner's private test.
family: Logan Calder is Lev’s second cousin. Lev brings a spare shopping bag. Logan chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Five missing lunches*, Logan says, “I changed the roster to save wages. Now I eat alone next to five imaginary people.”
connections: Nabil Reed. They need to open the porch post without destroying the dates hidden behind the wiring.

reactions.situation: A buyer offers extra for the porch lamp
reactions.response: Lev asks the owner whether the lamp is even part of the sale before discussing the offer.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Lev asks one close relative to check in privately instead of stopping the party for a public inquiry.
